pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 TYPES OF SENTENCES: INTERROGATIVE SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we use compound nouns when communicating?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify compound nouns in a text
2. use compound nouns in their singular and plural forms

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify compound nouns in a text
   In simple words: practise until you can identify compound nouns in a text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use compound nouns in their singular and plural forms
   In simple words: practise until you can use compound nouns in their singular and plural forms. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
4. Show that you can: identify compound nouns in a text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to an audio recording on human rights,
2. Write sentences using compound nouns in their singular and plural forms,
3. Communication and collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner work with peers categorise compound nouns
4. Self-efficacy: It is enhanced as the learner shows concerted attention to detail when forming separate and hyphenated compound nouns by combining two or more words.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify compound nouns in a text
2. use compound nouns in their singular and plural forms

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
